subject: EdgeCase AI committed plan: p95 headroom & dedicated slab mapping
messages:
From: Lydia Park <lydia@edgecase.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@edgecase.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — committed plan + p95 target

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the scoping call today. To recap EdgeCase's ask: we expect to move forward with a committed monthly token plan (starting Q3) and need Redwood to recommend a dedicated slab map that meets our p95 latency SLOs. High-level requirements below: 

- Committed volume: 150M tokens / month (phased to start at 40M month 1, 100M month 3)
- Traffic pattern: daily peak window ~ 18:00-20:00 PT, expected 30% of daily tokens in that 2-hr window; longer tail with occasional spikes up to ~2x baseline peak
- Target SLO: p95 generation latency <= 300ms for interactive endpoints (chat-style prompts, median prompt length ~120 tokens)
- Model mix: baseline serving on quantized 13B for cost sensitivity; fallback routes to a higher-quality 70B variant for 10% of requests (sampling) and for elevated traffic with latency-cost tradeoffs

Can you put together: (a) tokens/sec mapping to GPUs (by model type / quantization assumption), (b) p95 headroom needed for a 99th percentile day (2x spike), and (c) a recommended slab reservation + burst credit strategy? We have procurement on copy (Tom) and will need a formal SOW/quote after sizing.

Attaching a short CSV with our simplified traffic curve and a sample prompt set. Happy to hop on a quick call if you need clarifications.

Thanks,
Lydia
Head of Platform
EdgeCase AI

Attachment: edgecase-traffic-sample.csv (text/csv)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia@edgecase.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@edgecase.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — committed plan + p95 target

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear brief. We've started a quick sizing pass and I looped Marissa (capacity planning) and Ben (sales engineering) to validate numbers. Quick notes / ask list before we finalize slab recommendations:

1) Traffic distribution: can you confirm token-per-request distribution (we used 120 tokens/request median, 95th ~480 tokens/request for worst-case). If you have a 24-hour token histogram that helps tighten headroom.
2) Tail tolerance: do you want hard p95 <= 300ms as a strict SLA, or a blended SLO with a short-duration elevated tail allowance (e.g., p95 <= 300ms maintained 99% of days)?

Preliminary sizing (back-of-envelope):
- Assumptions: 13B quantized 4-bit: ~110 tokens/sec per A100-80GB equivalent GPU under our continuous-batching profile; 70B quantized 4-bit: ~28 tokens/sec per GPU (attention and KV-cache overhead).
- Peak tokens/sec estimate (from your numbers):
  * Monthly 150M -> daily avg ~5M -> baseline peak (2-hr window) = 30% of daily -> 1.5M tokens in 2 hours -> ~210 tokens/sec baseline peak.
  * 2x spike scenario (99th day): ~420 tokens/sec.

Using the per-GPU rates above, equivalent GPU counts (no headroom):
- Baseline (13B): 210 t/s / 110 t/s per GPU = 1.9 -> 2 GPUs
- 2x spike (13B): 420 / 110 = 3.8 -> 4 GPUs

This is optimistic because p95 latency requires headroom for batching inefficiencies and concurrency; we recommend keeping a 25-40% headroom buffer for p95 headroom depending on tail behavior. With a 30% headroom buffer:
- Baseline reserve: 2 * 1.3 -> ~3 GPUs
- Spike reserve (safety target): 4 * 1.3 -> ~5 GPUs

I'll hand to Marissa to run a more detailed simulation (model mix routing, fallback to 70B for sampled requests, and burst credits). Ben — please prepare a preliminary SOW outline and pricing per GPU slab for EdgeCase.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Park <lydia@edgecase.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Apr 2028 08:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — committed plan + p95 target

On Wed, Apr 11, 2028 at 11:02 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Preliminary sizing (back-of-envelope): ...

Thanks — ran a quick sim overlaying EdgeCase's sample curve and a modeled request mix. Key inputs I used (attached workbook 'edgecase-deal-sizing.xlsx' and exported sim 'p95_latency_sim.csv'):

- Model per-GPU sustained token rates (continuous batching):
  * 13B, q4: 110 t/s (A100-80GB equiv)
  * 70B, q4: 28 t/s
- Request mix: 90% routed to 13B baseline; 10% routed to 70B (sampling for quality). During spikes we add an emergency fallback: route up to 20% of baseline traffic to 13B if 70B capacity is saturated (configurable).
- Batching and concurrency assumptions: median batching gains reduce CPU/GPU overhead; but p95 is hurt by concurrency and cache warmup. I simulated warm-cache and cold-warm mixes (80/20).

Simulation outputs (rounded):
- Baseline peak (2-hr window): 210 t/s -> needs 3 GPUs of 13B to maintain p95 <= 300ms (includes 30% headroom).
- 2x spike day: 420 t/s -> needs 6 GPUs of 13B to keep p95 <= 300ms if no fallback.
- Mixed routing with 10% 70B sampling reduces 13B load by ~10% in nominal times -> baseline requirement drops to 2 GPUs, but p95 tail still needs the 30% buffer, so we recommend reserving 3 GPUs as baseline.

Recommended slab plan and burst strategy (deal-aligned):
1) Reserve a "core slab" of 4 A100-equivalent GPUs (13B q4) for the committed baseline. Rationale: gives nominal baseline coverage + 30% headroom and reduces risk for p95 tightness during slower cache-warm periods.
2) Add a 2-GPU burst slab (on the same dedicated pool) that can be auto-enabled during the 2-hr daily peak and by policy for short high-tail events. Burst can be metered and billed differently; if you prefer strict commit, convert burst slab to reserved capacity.
3) Keep a small cross-model fallback policy: if 70B warms slowly or saturates, route sampled requests to 13B and degrade quality gracefully. This reduces p95 pressure on 70B GPUs.
4) Operational playbook: pre-warm caches 15 minutes before daily peak window; run a canary traffic ramp for the first 2 weeks after go-live; set an automated rollback to hosted model variants if p95 breaches for >10 minutes continuously.

Cost/quote inputs (ballpark):
- Reserved slab: 4 GPUs (monthly reserved) + 2 GPU burst pool (on-demand style)
- Alternate conservative option: reserve 6 GPUs baseline (higher cost) to avoid any burst billing and to cap p95 risk at the cost of higher commit.

Attached: edgecase-deal-sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet with detailed per-minute sim)
Attached: p95_latency_sim.csv (export of p95 time series for the simulated 30-day window)

Let me know if you want me to run a scenario with 50% sampling to 70B (for quality-first use cases) or tighten headroom to 25%.

-Marissa
Senior Capacity Planner | Redwood Inference

Attachments: edgecase-deal-sizing.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), p95_latency_sim.csv (text/csv)

- Please prepare a one-page SOW with: reserved slab sizing (4 GPUs), burst buffer pricing (per-hour and monthly cap), fallback routing SLA language (p95 target and rollback triggers), and an expected timeline for pre-warm/canary.
- We will need SOC2 evidence for the dedicated pool and a note on data separation for the reserved slab in the SOW.

Ben — can you draft the SOW/quote and share by EOD Monday this week? If possible include an option to convert burst to reserved at month 3.
